Plaster Ceiling Price per Sq Ft Malaysia (2026): Quotation Guide

Published 20 November 2026

A flat plaster ceiling in Malaysia costs roughly RM5.50–12 per sq ft in 2026, supplied and installed, according to published contractor guides. L-boxes run at about RM15–28 per ft run, cove edges at RM18–30 per ft run, and cornice from about RM4 per ft run for a plain profile. Painting, wiring and LED strips are usually extra, so a good plaster ceiling quotation lists them as separate lines.

Plaster ceiling price per sq ft in Malaysia (2026)

“Plaster ceiling” in Malaysia almost always means gypsum board screwed to a metal frame under the slab, with taped joints and a skim coat. The flat ceiling is priced per square foot. Published rates vary by source, so here they are side by side:

Source (2026 unless stated) Flat ceiling Notes
plasterceiling.my RM5.50 per sq ft Contractor price list
Qanvast (Aug 2025) RM6.50–7.50 per sq ft Varies with materials and complexity
Hypro Renovation RM7–9 per sq ft Supply & install, KL area; 9mm board
ClickBina RM8–12 per sq ft Klang Valley, supply & install, excludes painting

Moisture-resistant board, used in kitchens and bathrooms, costs a little more: Hypro puts it at RM8.50–11 per sq ft. ClickBina suggests cement or calcium silicate board for wet areas.

What moves your rate up or down:

  • Ceiling height. ClickBina says scaffolding for ceilings above 10 ft adds 10–20% to labour.
  • Location and access. Hypro places KL at the upper end, Selangor suburbs in the middle and smaller towns such as Ipoh and Seremban at the lower end. Lift limits and parking also add time.
  • Board grade and brand. ClickBina puts branded boards at 15–30% more than generic ones.
  • Design. A two-tier or coffered ceiling runs at about RM22–35 per sq ft, and multi-tier feature ceilings at RM35–50 per sq ft, in ClickBina’s figures.

L-box, cove lighting and cornice: priced per foot run

Anything that follows the wall is measured in feet run (ft run), the length along the wall. Watch the unit when you compare quotes, because some contractors price the same work per sq ft of design area.

Item Published rate Unit Source
L-box / light trough RM15–28 per ft run Hypro
L-box RM25 per ft run plasterceiling.my
Cove (curved edge) RM18–30 per ft run Hypro
Perimeter cove / L-box with light channel RM15–25 per sq ft of design area ClickBina (LED separate)
Cornice, plain gypsum RM4–8 per ft run ClickBina
Cornice, profiled or ornate RM8–25 per ft run ClickBina
Bulkhead / beam boxing RM15–30 per ft run ClickBina

An L-box is the dropped box along the edge of the ceiling that hides wiring, pipes or a light strip. ClickBina gives a typical drop of 100–250mm. Cove lighting is the indirect light hidden in that channel.

Extras to quote as separate lines

Most published flat-ceiling rates cover the frame, board, joint taping and skim coat, and nothing else. Hypro lists wiring, downlight points, LED strips, the final paint and stripping an old ceiling as normally excluded. ClickBina prices these extras as follows:

Extra Published rate Unit
Downlight or fan cut-out (ceiling labour only) RM15–30 per cut-out
Cove LED strip, supply & install RM8–20 per ft run of cove
LED driver / transformer RM80–200 per zone
Electrician’s wiring RM120–250 per circuit
Hacking and disposal of old ceiling RM2–5 per sq ft

Heavy fittings are another hidden cost. Qanvast notes that ceilings sometimes need reinforcing for heavy fixtures, so ask about ceiling fans, chandeliers and cassette aircon units before you price.

How to measure for a plaster ceiling quotation

  1. Flat ceiling, per sq ft. Length × width of each room. A 20 × 15 ft living room is 300 sq ft. State whether you measure the full room or deduct the L-box area.
  2. L-box, cove and cornice, per ft run. For a full perimeter, 2 × (length + width). The same 20 × 15 ft room has 70 ft run of perimeter.
  3. Cut-outs and lighting. Count downlights, fan points and LED driver zones as numbered items, not as part of the sq ft rate.
  4. Wet areas separately. Put kitchen and bathroom ceilings on their own lines with the moisture-resistant board named.
  5. Existing ceiling. If an old ceiling has to come down first, add removal and disposal per sq ft.

Sample plaster ceiling quotation (illustrative)

This is an illustrative example for a condo living & dining room (20 × 15 ft), a master bedroom (12 × 14 ft) and a kitchen (8 × 10 ft). Every rate sits inside the published ranges above. Use your own rates.

Item Unit Qty Rate (RM) Amount (RM)
Living & dining: flat 9mm gypsum board ceiling on metal frame, taped & skimmed sq ft 300 9.00 2,700.00
Living & dining: L-box with light trough along perimeter ft run 70 22.00 1,540.00
Living & dining: cove LED strip, supply & install ft run 70 12.00 840.00
Living & dining: LED driver zone 2 120.00 240.00
Living & dining: downlight cut-outs nos 12 20.00 240.00
Master bedroom: flat 9mm gypsum board ceiling sq ft 168 9.00 1,512.00
Master bedroom: plain gypsum cornice ft run 52 6.00 312.00
Kitchen: remove & dispose of existing ceiling sq ft 80 3.00 240.00
Kitchen: flat moisture-resistant board ceiling sq ft 80 10.00 800.00
Total 8,424.00

Excluded: painting, electrical wiring and downlight fittings, scaffolding for ceilings above 10 ft, and management deposits. That works out to about RM15.37 per sq ft over the 548 sq ft of ceiling, well above the flat-ceiling rate, because the L-box, LED and cut-outs are where the money goes. That’s why a single per-sq-ft price for “plaster ceiling” so often leaves a contractor short.

What to write in the specification

  • Board: type and thickness (for example 9mm gypsum board, moisture-resistant board in wet areas), and the brand if the client cares.
  • Frame: metal furring or a suspended grid. ClickBina recommends galvanised steel C-channel at 600mm centres over timber.
  • Finish: joint taping and how many skim coats. ClickBina suggests two passes as a minimum.
  • Painting: included or not, and how many coats.
  • Timeline: ClickBina puts a 100–150 sq ft room at 1–2 days for framing, boarding and jointing, plus 1–2 days for skim and sanding after drying, and a whole apartment at 5–10 working days.
  • Exclusions and validity: wiring, light fittings, scaffolding and how long the price holds.

If the client adds an L-box or more downlights after approving the quote, price the change in writing with a variation order before the boards go up.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a plaster ceiling per sq ft in Malaysia in 2026?
Published 2026 contractor guides put a flat gypsum board ceiling at roughly RM5.50 to RM12 per sq ft, supplied and installed, usually excluding painting. Moisture-resistant board for kitchens and bathrooms costs a little more, at around RM8.50 to RM11 per sq ft in one Klang Valley guide.
How much does an L-box ceiling cost?
L-boxes are usually priced per foot run along the wall. 2026 guides put them at roughly RM15 to RM28 per ft run, and cove edges at about RM18 to RM30 per ft run. Some contractors price the same work per sq ft of design area instead, so check the unit before comparing quotes.
Is painting included in a plaster ceiling price?
Usually not. Most published rates cover the frame, board, joint taping and skim coat, with the final paint, wiring, LED strips and removal of an old ceiling quoted separately. Say clearly in your quotation which of these you include.
How long does it take to install a plaster ceiling?
One 2026 guide puts a single room of 100 to 150 sq ft at 1 to 2 days for framing, boarding and jointing, plus another 1 to 2 days for skim coat and sanding after drying. A whole apartment takes about 5 to 10 working days.
How do you measure a plaster ceiling for a quotation?
Measure the flat ceiling in square feet (length × width of each room). Measure L-boxes, cove edges and cornice in feet run along the wall, which for a full perimeter is 2 × (length + width). Count downlight cut-outs and LED driver zones as separate items.
